title: Word Break
prompt:
Given a string `s` and a dictionary `wordDict`, return `true` if `s` can be split into a sequence of one or more dictionary words. Words may be reused.

**Example**: `s = "applepenapple"`, `wordDict = ["apple","pen"]` → `true`. `s = "catsandog"`, `wordDict = ["cats","dog","sand","and","cat"]` → `false`.

**Constraints**: `1 <= s.length <= 300`, `1 <= wordDict.length <= 1000`, words have length 1–20.
hints: Greedily taking the longest (or shortest) matching word can paint you into a corner. If you knew which *prefixes* of s can be split, how would you decide about a longer prefix?
Let dp[i] = the first i characters can be split. dp[0] = true. dp[i] is true if some split j < i has dp[j] true and `s[j..i)` is a word.
Put the words in a `HashSet`, then `if (dp[j] && dict.contains(s.substring(j, i))) { dp[i] = true; break; }`

solution.explanation: Any valid split of the first i characters ends with a word `s[j..i)` right after a valid split of the first j characters. Trying every j therefore checks every possibility, and the whole string's answer is dp[n]. O(n²) substring checks, each O(n) to build and hash, so O(n³) worst case; O(n) space.
